title: OSPFv2 Passive Interfaces and Neighbor Control
summary: Suppress unnecessary OSPFv2 Hello transmissions on access LAN segments while maintaining link-state route advertisements and transit neighbor adjacencies.
learning_objectives: Explain the security risks and resource inefficiencies of sending OSPFv2 Hello packets to edge LAN segments
Configure individual interface suppression using the passive-interface command under the OSPF router process
Implement an enterprise security best practice using passive-interface default followed by targeted no passive-interface exclusions
Verify that passive interfaces suppress Hello packet transmission while continuing to advertise connected subnets into the Link-State Database (LSDB)
Verify that transit router neighbor adjacencies remain in the FULL state across active point-to-point links
Verify end-to-end data plane reachability across interconnected multi-hop OSPF networks
Analyze the operational impact of inadvertently making a transit link passive through negative failure injection

source.origin: Independently authored enterprise OSPFv2 interface security curriculum guide aligned with Cisco CCNA exam topic 3.2
